national_raw_news.content: In a historic ceremony held against the grand backdrop of the Statue of Unity in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, President Droupadi Murmu presented the 72nd National Film Awards, honouring cinematic excellence for the year 2024 across feature, non-feature, and writing categories. A total of 92 awardees were recognized during the event. Legendary actor Anant Nag was honoured with the prestigious Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024 for his outstanding contribution to Indian cinema spanning over five decades. In the feature film section, the political thriller Article 370 bagged the Swarna Kamal for Best Feature Film. Director Randeep Hooda received the Best Debut Director award for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar, while Nag Ashwin Singireddy’s sci-fi film Kalki 2898 AD won the award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Rajkumar Periasamy received the Best Direction trophy for the Tamil movie Amaran. The Telugu film 35- Chinna Katha Kaadu took home the Best Children’s Film honor. In the acting categories, the Best Actor in a Leading Role award was jointly presented to veteran actor Mammootty for Bramayugam and Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion. Yami Gautam won the Best Actress in a Leading Role award for her performance in Article 370. Sanjay Mishra secured the Best Supporting Actor award for Bhakshak, while the Best Supporting Actress title was shared by Sachana Namidass for Maharaja and Ropashree Varkady for Mithya. In the non-feature section, Marathi film Bhangaar won the Best Non-Feature Film award, while director Aanand L Rai won Best Direction for his work Statue of Unity – Ekta ka Prateek. In the writing on cinema categories, Sanjeev Shrivastava bagged the Swarna Kamal for Best Film Critic. Bollywood actor Kartik Aaryan expressed his deep gratitude upon receiving his first National Film Award for Chandu Champion. He described the honour as a milestone in his artistic journey. Addressing the film fraternity, President Droupadi Murmu today highlighted the cultural strength and diversity of Indian cinema. The President emphasised the important role of cinema in reflecting India’s varied languages, traditions and social experiences. She said that films not only entertain audiences but also connect people across regions and help showcase India’s rich cultural heritage. In his address, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw congratulated all the award winners and acknowledged the contribution of technicians, cinematographers and other members working behind the scenes. He also congratulated the winner of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, Anant Nag, and appreciated his contribution to the film world spanning more than five decades. The Minister said that the idea of taking the National Film Awards to different tourist destinations draws inspiration from India’s G20 presidency, when more than 200 meetings were held in over 60 cities across the country. Mr Vaishnaw invited all States and Union Territories to identify an important tourist destination in their respective regions so that they can host a future edition of the National Film Awards.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 78 India condemns Pakistani airstrikes on Afghanistan’s Kunar and Paktika provinces
national_raw_news.content: India has strongly condemned Pakistan’s airstrikes on Afghanistan in its Kunar and Paktika provinces. Addressing media in New Delhi this evening, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said such instances of aggression against a sovereign neighbour go against regional peace and security. He reaffirmed New Delhi’s steadfast support for Afghanistan, its independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, as also for the welfare and well-being of its people. The spokesperson offered condolences on the civilian lives lost in the airstrikes and wished for speedy recovery of the injured. On Pakistan’s Field Marshal Asim Munir’s statement that Pakistan’s armed forces remain determined to defeat terrorism, Mr Jaiswal said Pakistan needs to demonstrate action and firm commitment. He stated that Islamabad must take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes in what they say. On Pakistan’s ruling by the Court of Arbitration on Indus Water Treaty, Mr Jasiwal said the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration, as sought to be projected by Pakistan, but by an illegally constituted Court. He said India sees this as just one more attempt by Pakistan at distorting the reality. He stated that Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda. Replying to another query, the spokesperson informed that External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar met with his Ukrainian counterpart yesterday. In this meeting, Dr Jaishankar discussed the recent developments in the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The External Affairs Minister once again put forth India’s point that dialogue and diplomacy is the way forward for peaceful resolution. The spokesperson added that India is in touch with both sides and have told them that India is ready to contribute in any way that it can. He expressed India’s hope that there will be a peaceful resolution of the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. On India-Bangladesh ties, Mr Jaiswal said that India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh. He said New Delhi is ready to discuss all bilateral issues within the structured mechanisms.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 378 Amit Shah Calls for Decisive Action to Dismantle Drug Networks, Says Govt Targets Drug-Free India...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that the time has come to take a strong and decisive blow to narcotics, which has become a serious threat to the country and the world. Inaugurating the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States and UTs in New Delhi today, Mr Shah said, with the aim of improving the welfare of the youth, Government has prepared the roadmap 2029. He said, by 2029 Government will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India. The Home Minister said, the roadmap of drug-free India is very important to achieve Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s goal of creating a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He said, in this fight against drugs, India is moving towards complete victory by setting targets , timeline and accountability. Mr Shah said, now there is a need to go from Meeting to Mission, Reporting to Result, Seizure to End of Network and Case to Conviction. He said, the goal should be to make ANTF an Anti-Narco Mission Command. The Minister called upon officers to move forward with the aim of dismantling the network instead of a Seizure-centric approach. He said, district will have to be made the basic unit of fight against drugs. Mr Shah informed that Nashamukt Mitras will visit 10 lakh schools, colleges and institutions of the country to create awareness among the youth and sensitize the campus directors. He said, along with backwards-forward investigation, financial investigation and finding digital links should be the priority. The Home Minister said, the cartel has to be attacked at three levels, entry point, interstate distribution system and local cell network in the districts. He said, a campaign will have to be launched to send back the foreign accused present in India and blacklist them, so that they cannot come to India again. He added that the fugitives who are supplying drugs to the country from abroad should be caught and brought before the Indian courts. The Home Minister asked officers to make the entire process of converting every ANTF information into actionable intelligence a part of the state’s police culture. During the event, Mr Shah also launched the new website of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). He released four Television Commercials to create awareness among people about drug abuse. Mr Shah also laid the foundation stones for the new zonal office and residential complex of the NCB in Lucknow and a new zonal office complex in Dehradun. The two-day conference serves as a powerful platform to safeguard future generations from the menace of drugs. Heads of ANTFs from 36 States and Union Territories are attending the conference, being organised by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). Based on the theme of the United Resolve, Shared Responsibility, the conference is focusing on progress of targets assigned to State and UTs ANTFs in recently released Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-29).

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Sports 35 Asian Games: Indian Women’s Cricket Team Wins Country’s First Gold in Aichi-Nagoya, Medal Tally R...
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Women’s Cricket team reasserted its continental dominance by clinching a second successive gold medal at the Asian Games, thrashing Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final at Nisshin in Japan today. Opting to bat, India posted 216 for the loss of three wickets in the stipulated 20 overs, the highest total in Asian Games history, riding on Smriti Mandhana’s 79 runs off 45 balls and Richa Ghosh’s 48 off 22. In reply, Sri Lanka were bowled out for just 69 in 15.4 overs. This is India’s first gold medal at the ongoing Asiad and overall seventh medal. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the Women’s Cricket Team on the feat. Calling it a splendid triumph for Indian cricket, Mr Modi said that this victory also brings India its first Gold of this edition of the Games. In a social media post, he said that it was a commanding performance marked by confidence, skill, and wonderful teamwork. The Prime Minister said that the team has made the nation proud and will inspire countless young cricketers across the country. Indian men’s Badminton team defeated hosts Japan in the quarterfinals and assured itself of a medal at the Asian Games. Lakshya Sen was staring at defeat after losing the opening game and trailing 14-19 in the decider. However, Lakshya made a comeback, reeling off seven straight points to beat world No.7 and two-time world championships silver-medallist Kodai Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19 to give India a 1-0 lead. Playing the first doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have won two titles this season, registered a 21-18, 24-22 win over former world champions Hoki Takuro and Kobayashi Yugo to extend India’s lead to 2-0. Ayush Shetty then produced an impressive performance to see off world no. 16 Koki Watanabe 21-10 21-19 to seal the match and a medal for India. The Indian men were the silver-medallists of the last edition. In Wushu, India’s Roshibina Devi also confirmed a medal at the Asian Games after securing a 5-0 win over Chu Man Sin of Macao, in the Women’s 60kg quarterfinals. Roshibina, the 2018 and 2022 Asiad medallist, has now secured a third continental medal with another strong performance to advance to the semifinals. Roshibina will now be in action in the semifinals tomorrow for a place in the final. She is already a silver medallist from the 2023 Asian Games, when she came second in the Sanda 60 kg category. She also bagged a bronze medal in the 2018 Jakarta Games in the same weight category. Apart from her, India’s Aryan also moved to the quarterfinals as he fights for a medal. Aryan defeated Afghanistan’s Safi Shahzada in the Men’s 56kg pre-quarters 2-0 to progress into the quarterfinals. Indian boxer Jadumani Singh defeated Nepal’s Chandra Bahadur Thapa to march into the pre-quarters in the Men’s 55kg preliminary round at the Nishio Gymnasium in Japan today. Commonwealth Games silver medallist Jadumani registered a unanimous 5-0 win over the reigning World Championships’ bronze medallist Thapa with a brilliant bout. Jadumani will now be up against Filipino boxer Carlo Paalam in the pre-quarters on Saturday. Paalam is a silver medallist from the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games. Earlier, Glasgow Games gold medallist Sakshi Chaudhary defeated Paris Olympics bronze medallist Aira Villegas in the preliminary round at the Asian Games 2026 to march into the pre-quarters. Sakshi outclassed the Filipino pugilist by a unanimous decision of 5-0. She will be facing current 51kg world champion Alua Balkibekova on Thursday. In Men’s Cricket, India narrowly avoided a historic upset, defeating hosts Japan by two runs in a rain-curtailed, five-overs-a-side one-off T20 International match at the Sano International Cricket Ground today. This was India’s 200th victory in T20 Internationals, including Super Over wins. After a nearly 2.5-hour delay due to a wet outfield, India skipper Shreyas Iyer won the toss and opted to bat first. However, Japan’s spinners made the most of the conditions, restricting the visitors to 32 for 4 after five overs. Chasing 33 off 30 balls, Japan gave India a major scare and came agonisingly close to pulling off one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history. national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 168 Centre inks deals with 21 States, UTs for next phase of UDAN scheme
national_raw_news.content: Twenty-one states and Union Territories have signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoU) with the Civil Aviation Ministry under the next phase of the UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) scheme in New Delhi today. Speaking on the occasion, Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu described UDAN as one of the most revolutionary schemes in the country, propelling regional air connectivity across the nation. Highlighting the vision for the next phase, the Minister noted that following the extension of the scheme for another 10 years, the government aims to construct 100 new airports and 200 modern heliports or helipads across the country. He added that the upcoming phase targets facilitating travel for four crore UDAN passengers. Mr Naidu also noted that the aviation-sector jobs have grown from around 3 million in 2014 to nearly 7.7 million today, with the potential to reach 25 million by 2040. Mr Naidu stated that more than 90 airports have been built over the past decade under UDAN, extending affordable air travel benefits to nearly one crore 54 lakh passengers. The event also witnessed the launch of the Challenge Mode Portal for Aerodrome Development and the release of the Scheme Document for the next phase of UDAN Route bidding. Under the Challenge Mode, airport projects will be prioritized and fast-tracked to cut construction timelines down to an 18-month target from the earlier average of two to three years. The route bidding round process will facilitate the expansion of air services to unserved and underserved regions, improving accessibility and mobility and supporting wider economic activity, tourism, trade and employment.

national_raw_news.title: Maharashtra CM Announces Immediate Assistance for Farmers Affected by Drought-Like Situation 48 mins ago 26
national_raw_news.content: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis today said the state government will provide immediate assistance to farmers affected by the drought-like situation without waiting for financial assistance from the Centre. He said a preliminary notification on drought mitigation is expected to be issued by Saturday. Addressing reporters after a Cabinet meeting in Mumbai, Mr Fadnavis said panchnamas to assess crop losses will begin from tomorrow. Soybean, maize and cotton have suffered the most damage, while paddy cultivation in the Konkan region has also been affected. The Chief Minister also announced a Cabinet sub-committee headed by Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule to take speedy decisions on relief measures. The committee will have Cabinet powers, with Chief Secretary Rajesh Agarwal as its member-secretary. Mr Fadnavis said ministers and public representatives will visit affected areas from tomorrow to assess the situation and interact with farmers. He said the state will separately prepare a proposal seeking financial assistance from the Centre under National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) norms. He stressed that drinking water and fodder for livestock will receive special attention, with arrangements to be planned for the next seven to eight months in coordination with local bodies. The drought-like conditions are particularly affecting parts of Marathwada and Vidarbha following weak monsoon rainfall.
